name: Capital One Financial

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Lends mostly through credit cards (74% of Q3 net revenue), plus auto loans and bank deposits; since May 2025 it also owns the Discover, PULSE and Diners Club payment networks.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: Q3 net revenue $16.3B: Credit Card 74%, Consumer Banking 20%, Commercial Banking 6%. Net interest income $12.9B (79% of revenue), non-interest income $3.5B. Network volume $190.9B in Q3.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Mostly US consumers and small business: $276.4B card loans, $94.0B consumer banking (auto $92.9B), $92.1B commercial. No single-customer concentration disclosed; the risk is large merchants on Discover/PULSE that could demand lower fees (10-K risk factor).

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: Overwhelmingly US; UK (Capital One Europe plc) and a Canadian branch run card businesses, and network services are offered globally. Revenue by country and currency exposure not broken out in the pages read.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Spread lender: earns interest on card and auto loans, pays little on deposits (2.94% on interest-bearing). NIM 8.41% (+40bp QoQ). 79% of revenue is net interest income, 21% fees and interchange. Plus network fees as owner of Discover.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Efficiency ratio 54.2% (adjusted 48.8%); marketing $1.6B in Q3 (about 10% of revenue). Credit losses are the big variable cost: NCOs $3.1B (2.73% rate). Integration spend $338M Discover + $47M Brex in Q3 ($2.4B cumulative Discover). No synergy target or delivery figure found in the 10-K, 10-Q or earnings release.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Inputs are money and rails, not goods. Deposits $480.7B (signal tags fed_funds, 2y: rate +3bp QoQ to 2.94%); wholesale funding and securitisation (senior notes $36.3B, borrowings $49.8B; tag hy_spreads, HY OAS 3.72% widening); regulatory capital (CET1 13.8% vs 9.0% minimum; tag regulation); merchant acceptance for Discover/PULSE (single point of failure; 10-K names Reg II interchange cap as the threat to network synergies). Pass-through: card pricing reprices with rates and NIM rose 40bp, so cost increases are largely passed on; deposit beta not published. Technology vendors: nothing found in pages read.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Scale in card (domestic card loans $260B), data-driven underwriting, direct-bank deposits, and now its own network: Global Payment Network volume $190.9B in Q3 (+25% YoY). Different now: legacy Capital One debit cards reissued onto the network (10-K: substantially complete), plus Brex business cards ($4.5B deal).

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Household name in cards and auto loans; marketing $4.75B in 9M 2026 = 10.0% of revenue. Customers would notice if it vanished, but cards are easy to switch; pricing power shows in 17.75% card revenue margin.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Rivals: JPM/Chase, Citi, AXP, SYF, Visa, Mastercard. Q3 purchase volume $254.7B (+11% YoY) and loans +4% YoY; peer share data not compared in detail. Quarter-on-quarter purchase volume was flat ($253.8B to $254.7B).

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Loans $462.5B (+4% YoY, +1% QoQ). Levers: network volume (+25% YoY), debit migration, Brex, auto +11% YTD. Network synergy value is not quantified in filings read, and the 10-K says a Reg II cap on three-party debit would remove most of it.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: CET1 13.8% (vs 9.0% required; 14.4% a year ago). Bought back $2.6B in Q3 at $209.63 average ($7.9B in 9M; $6.2B left on $16B plan), about 15% above today's $182.52; shares 601.5M vs 635.7M. TBV/share $102.72, down 2% YoY as AOCI loss widened to $10.0B. Founder-CEO Fairbank. Pay design and insider ownership table in 2026 proxy not read in detail.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Not losing relevance: purchase volume +11%, network volume +25%. Risks: credit cycle, Reg II/interchange rules, Discover merchant acceptance, key-person (Fairbank, founder). 9M GAAP ROTCE 17.0%; Q4 2025 was 9.7% (Discover charges), showing the swing.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: No 4.01/4.02/NT filings and no material weakness (EY clean ICFR opinion FY2025). But: inherited CFPB order (to Dec 2030) and Fed order (Apr 2025) from Discover card misclassification, SEC investigation of that matter, shareholder suit, savings-account class action and NY AG suit. Adjusted EPS $6.69 vs GAAP $5.61 (19% gap, mostly deal amortisation $483M and integration $385M pre-tax).

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Boom +: loan growth, low losses. Overheat 0: NIM up and credit benign but deposit costs rising (+3bp QoQ) with Fed leaning to hike. Stagflation -: squeezed borrowers. Slowdown -: card losses and reserve builds; HY OAS 3.72% (+105bp since August) while reserve coverage fell to 4.92% from 5.21%.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Inherited consent orders (CFPB, Fed) bind COF; interchange antitrust settlement final hearing was set for Nov 16 2026 (outcome not checked); Reg II debit cap is the key network risk. The brief says the Eighth Circuit vacated the cap on Oct 26; I did not verify that in a primary source.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Price $182.52 (2026-11-25), TBV $102.72: P/TBV 1.78x. At 10% cost of equity and 3% growth that implies ROTCE 15.5% (0% growth: 17.8%). Actual ROTCE: Q3 21.1%, 9M 17.0% GAAP, FY2025 adjusted 18.5%; but Q1 2026 12.2%, Q4 2025 9.7%. Cushion is thin on GAAP, modest on adjusted. P/E 11.2x TTM GAAP EPS $16.35 (8.8x TTM adjusted $20.78). Own year-end P/TBV approx 1.0-2.2x (2025 2.21x exact; earlier years estimated from XBRL). Peers: JPM 2.81x (ROTCE 20%), SYF 1.61x (ROTCE 25.2%). Year range $174.24-259.64.

status_reason: Quality B but the cushion is thin (P/TBV 1.78x implies 15.5% ROTCE vs 17.0% 9M GAAP, which includes a $225M reserve release) and the 'network value' mistake is unproven: no synergy target or network revenue figure is disclosed in the filings read, and the Reg II ruling is unverified.

feedback.fact: Domestic card 30+ day delinquency 3.87% in Oct 2026 (Oct 2025 3.99% per industry file); Q3 total 30+ delinquency 3.41% vs 3.50% a year earlier; Q3 NCO rate 2.73% vs 3.16%. Q3 delinquency rose 27bp QoQ (seasonal). Allowance coverage fell to 4.92% from 5.21% a year ago with a $225M release.
feedback.effect: Credit is benign in the data, contradicting the Slowdown pricing in markets; supports late-Overheat hard-data read, but reserve release plus HY OAS 3.72% leaves less buffer if the turn comes.

feedback.fact: Interest-bearing deposit rate 2.94% (+3bp QoQ); NIM 8.41% (+40bp); Q3 purchase volume $254.7B, flat QoQ and +11% YoY.
feedback.effect: Confirms rising deposit costs but strong pricing; spending flat QoQ is consistent with flat real consumer spending in October.

coverage_notes.10-K: FY2025 10-K read selectively: auditor and ICFR report, risk factors on network synergies and Reg II, business description. Segment and geography detail not read in full.
coverage_notes.10-Q: Q3 2026 10-Q read selectively (MD&A highlights, segments, repurchases, legal note, Brex note). Q2, Q1 and Q4 2025 data taken from the 5-quarter tables in the Q3 financial supplement, not from the filings.
coverage_notes.earnings_release: Q3 2026 release (EX-99.1) and financial supplement (EX-99.2) read; adjusted EPS reconciliation included.
coverage_notes.presentation: Earnings slide deck not found among the Oct 20 8-K exhibits I opened; the Nov 10 8-K (Item 7.01) exhibit was not located. Discover synergy targets and debit-migration progress beyond the 10-K statement were therefore not found.
coverage_notes.ir_fact_sheet: Financial supplement is EX-99.2 of the Q3 8-K (covered); separate IR-site fact sheet not fetched.
coverage_notes.def14a: 2026 proxy read only for FY2025 ROTCE and adjusted metrics and ownership section; pay design and insider ownership table not studied. Form 4 trades not checked.
coverage_notes.red_flag_scan: EDGAR 8-K list Nov 2025 to Nov 2026 shows no Items 4.01, 4.02 or NT filings; 5.02 filings Nov 2025, Feb 2026, Apr 2026 not read. CORRESP/UPLOAD letters exist in 2024-Jan 2025; content not read, none found since.
coverage_notes.price: yFinance last close 2026-11-25 $182.52. SYF and JPM TBV and ROTCE from their Q3 releases; AXP TBV not extracted. Own historical P/TBV approximated from XBRL equity minus goodwill, intangibles and preferred for 2020-24.
coverage_notes.unverified_context: Eighth Circuit ruling on Oct 26 and Berkshire stake cut come from the brief, not from a primary source I read.
